terminology:
Policy category is "learners who experience barriers to learning", a deliberately broad framing
White Paper 6 chose "barriers to learning and development" over "special education needs"
SIAS domain "Communication" is scoped to little or no functional speech, requiring AAC
No DLD or SLI category in SIAS; CATALISE terms appear in SA research, not in school policy
identificationCriteria: Not established from the sources consulted for this entry — no national diagnostic or eligibility criteria were identified. The dominant constraint reported in the literature is not the criteria but the assessment tools available to apply them — see below. If you work in this system, this is exactly the field to fill in.
assessments:
The central documented problem
Shortage of valid tools for multilingual populations, and for several SA languages
Tests in use are built on European and American contexts, with guidance that does not fit
Language sample analysis used as a partial response to the missing norms
multilingualProvision:
Multilingualism is the whole problem — 11 official spoken languages, plus SASL
HPCSA requires cultural competence; parts of the workforce reportedly do not meet it
Shortage of therapists fluent in African languages; ad hoc translation used as a stopgap
Less experienced therapists more often able to work in African languages — a pipeline issue
referralPathway:
Under SIAS, screening starts at school level with the School-Based Support Team
Escalating to the District-Based Support Team where the school cannot meet the need
District support may include remedial work, assessment, devices, therapy or placement
SLT is one option in a graduated response, not an entitlement in itself
serviceModel:
Speech-language therapists in public health facilities and private practice
An ongoing professional debate about SLT roles in schools (SAJCD)
Practitioners report private practice 66%, mainstream school 51% (COST survey, 2017)
They name urban/rural 88%, cost to parents 85%, income 78% as shaping access
legalEntitlement:
Runs through inclusive-education policy rather than through a diagnosis
Education White Paper 6 (2001) set the national inclusive-education strategy
SIAS (2014) operationalises it — identifying barriers and allocating support
Entitlement attaches to assessed support need under SIAS, not to a diagnosis
funding:
One case per practitioner, more than one funder allowed — COST IS1406 2017, n = 82
Funders: family 56%, private health insurance 21%, state education 18%, state health 13%
15% said a maximum number of sessions applied (n = 82)
workforce:
Registration and regulation by the Health Professions Council of South Africa
A shortage of therapists overall is consistently reported
And specifically of therapists who speak the African languages of the children they serve
